answer: Every tow horse is branded and its miles are logged by the tow master for each journey along the canal, and the register holds the brand of each horse. A island horse hired from a dealer fails the register: at the juniper of the towpath the brand must match the master's own iron, and a dealer's horse bears another mark. Forging the register means keeping horses for a year, bribing a tow master and paying 12,100, while the wander entry in the register is checked at every milepost, so a horse whose miles were never logged is unhitched at the next bridge.
